full_judgment:
4. No oral evidence was led by any of the parties since there was no controversy as to the loss or non-delivery of one case as alleged by the plaintiff. The controversy involves the interpredation of the jurisdiction clause and the 'Gold Clause' of the bill of lading by which limitation of liability of the carrier for loss of a package the value of which was not declared, was provided. The learned Subordinate Judge held that he had jurisdiction to try the suit and that the ship owner was liable to pay to the consignee the value of £100/- pound (gold sovereign) in Pakistani currency i.e. the value of 67+ tolas of gold, in the then price in Pakistan and he accordingly decreed a sum of Rs. 9450/ against the ship owner, being the value of 671 tolas of gold, i.e. the weight of 100 gold sovereign, each piece weighing 11 annas. 

 7. It has been argued that the liability for loss of each package whose value has not been declared in the bill of lading is limited to Rs. 1320 (Pakistani currency) being the equivalent of £100/- of English currency at the then exchange rate. The learned Advocate has strenuously argued that the words "or the equivalent of that sum in other currency" in Rule 5 of Articles IV of Hague Rules which are applicable to the Bill of Lading clearly shows £,100/- is a sum of English currency. The relevant clauses in- Hague Rules with regard to the limitation of liability for loss of each package are contained in Rule 5 of Article IV and Article IX.
